clue.text: The King had a great dinner cooked for Milner's young men

parts.note: K is the standard abbreviation for king, as on chess pieces and playing cards

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal banquet is laid on for a group of young men attached to a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals the rearrangement of the two words that follow 'a'. Milner's Kindergarten was the nickname for the young Oxford men Alfred Milner gathered to run South Africa after the Boer War.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname given to Lord Milner's band of young administrators in South Africa was this word for an infants' school.

clue.text: The expertise to recognize the sound of Julia Ward

parts.note: to recognize someone is to know them

indicators.note: the sound of a name means a word pronounced the same way is wanted

parts.note: Julia Ward Howe was the American poet who wrote the Battle Hymn of the Republic

explanation.surface: Someone claims the skill to identify the voice of a famous American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound of' works on the poet's surname: Julia Ward Howe, author of the Battle Hymn of the Republic, is pronounced like the question word.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical skill or technical knowledge in a field is commonly called this, so it is a synonym for expertise.

clue.text: Organ getting the right wind

parts.note: the nose is an organ of the body, used for smelling

explanation.surface: A church organ is being supplied with the correct air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a musical instrument fed by wind, but it is the body organ, the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call a strong headwind, one blowing straight on the bow, by this name.

clue.text: Sophia, for instance, can make her cross

explanation.surface: A woman called Sophia has the power to annoy her.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophia of Hanover, mother of George I, held this title. Read as 'female elector', the word also means a woman who may mark her X on a ballot paper, so 'make her cross' is voting, not angering.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a German prince-elector bore this title, as Sophia of Hanover did, and literally it also means a woman with a vote.

clue.text: Flout order one hears to change sides

indicators.note: what one hears is a spoken word, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: a sail or boom swinging to the other side of a boat jibes, given as an order to the crew

explanation.surface: Someone defies a command they hear to switch allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' marks the sailing word as a helmsman's command, 'Jibe!', to swing the sail across. Said aloud it matches the spelling with G.
explanation.definitionFit: To gibe is to taunt or mock, much as flouting treats something with open contempt.

clue.text: Assign new duties — a wheeze to support broken reed

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits below it, so it comes second
a broken thing has its parts out of place, so the letters of this word are rearranged

parts.note: a wheeze is British slang for a clever scheme or ploy

explanation.surface: Someone gives a fragile reed a new job, propping it up with a crafty trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges REED into REDE; 'to support' places PLOY beneath it in this down entry. A wheeze in British usage is a scheme, not a breathing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeploy troops or staff is to move them to fresh positions or jobs.

clue.text: Permission to be absent in Latin

definitions.text: Permission to be absent in Latin

parts.words: Permission to be absent in Latin
parts.note: a school or college pass to go away is a Latin word meaning let him go out

explanation.surface: A request for leave is phrased in an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: British boarding schools and Oxbridge colleges grant this leave of absence; the word is Latin for 'let him go out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave granted to a pupil or student to be away from school or college for a time is known by this Latin term.

clue.text: Harsh step, but not heartless

parts.note: a long step is a stride

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of this word is taken away

explanation.surface: A grating footstep, though it is not without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle letter of the little word 'not'; 'but' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or sound is loud and grating, which is harsh.

clue.text: Prepared for putting on salads

explanation.surface: Salad leaves have been made ready to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is golf, not placing: golf greens are prepared surfaces for putting.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting surfaces on a golf course share their name with leafy vegetables eaten as salad.

clue.text: Litter off Whitstable, perhaps, at the bottom of the sea

definitions.text: Litter off Whitstable, perhaps, at the bottom of the sea

parts.words: Litter off Whitstable, perhaps, at the bottom of the sea
parts.note: litter is read as bedding, a place where shellfish lie on the seabed near a Kent harbour famous for them

explanation.surface: Rubbish has piled up on the seabed off a Kent seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish, but a litter is also a bed; Whitstable in Kent is famous for its shellfish beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabed area where molluscs are bred or grow naturally, as at Whitstable, gets this name.

clue.text: Salesman leaves watch for the consumer

indicators.note: a word that leaves another is removed from it

parts.note: a repeater is a watch that chimes the time when a button is pressed
a rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A salesman departs from his post, which is good news for the customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes REP from the front of REPEATER; 'watch' is the chiming timepiece, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats food consumes it, so an eater is a consumer.

clue.text: The answer to this lies in the retort

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the run of these words

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter suggests the solution sits in a sharp reply, or in a laboratory flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lies in' marks the letters inside tHE RETOrt. 'The answer' plays on a crossword answer and the reply a retort is.
explanation.definitionFit: This formal word means to this matter or document, as in the papers attached.

clue.text: Old fighter with fiery temper

explanation.surface: A veteran boxer is known for losing his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Supermarine wartime aircraft shares its name with a hot-tempered person.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous British wartime fighter aircraft, and a word for someone quick to anger and fierce.

clue.text: Getting nearer, we hear, to Kent coast town

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so a word pronounced alike is wanted

parts.note: in the hide-and-seek game you are told you are warmer when getting closer to the target

explanation.surface: A traveller is approaching a seaside town in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the town in Kent near Deal, with its castle, sounds like 'warmer', the children's-game word for getting close.
explanation.definitionFit: A small seaside town beside Deal on the Kent coast, known for its Tudor castle.

clue.text: Guiding principle for a store lad, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given may form something other than what they spell

explanation.surface: A boy working in a shop needs some rule to live by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges STORE LAD; the anagram is presented as what the definition might stand for.
explanation.definitionFit: A star used to steer by, such as the Pole Star, and so figuratively a principle that guides one's actions.

clue.text: Game in which the players have to circulate

definitions.text: Game in which the players have to circulate

parts.words: Game in which the players have to circulate
parts.note: a bat-and-ball game where batters run a circuit of bases, like mingling guests at a party

explanation.surface: A party game where guests must mingle.
explanation.walkthrough: A British schoolchildren's bat-and-ball game, like baseball, in which a batter runs round four posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Its players score by running round a ring of posts after hitting the ball, so they literally circulate.

clue.text: Dark suit appropriate for this establishment?

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day
clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: A black outfit might be just the thing to wear to a certain venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark suit' reads as evening clothes, but it splits into time of darkness and card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-opening venue for drinking and dancing is a type of business establishment.

clue.text: Boy's projector in carrier, perhaps

explanation.surface: A lad's slide projector is in a shopping bag.
explanation.walkthrough: A schoolboy's forked stone-thrower, and the device that launches aircraft from a carrier's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A Y-shaped elastic stone thrower, and the steam launcher that flings planes off an aircraft carrier deck.

clue.text: On and off, he collects

parts.note: on and off are the two halves of a cricket field, and he is a man; together a church helper who takes the collection

explanation.surface: Someone gathers things intermittently.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the on side and the off side, so 'On and off' gives sides and 'he' a man: a churchwarden's assistant who takes the collection plate round.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant to a churchwarden in the Church of England, who shows people to pews and takes up the collection.

clue.text: Plaintiff has very strong inside experience

indicators.note: inside puts one piece within the other

parts.note: a plaintiff sues in court, so is a suer
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud or strong

explanation.surface: A litigant in court has a powerful inner experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' does the containing and 'has' just links; in music ff, fortissimo, marks a very loud passage, read here as very strong.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer something is to undergo or go through it, which is to experience it.

clue.text: A philistine city attracting a girl

parts.note: Gath was one of the five cities of the Philistines in the Bible, home of Goliath

explanation.surface: An uncultured town draws in a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'philistine' looks like 'uncultured', but it is the biblical people; Gath was their city. 'attracting' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as of the crime writer Christie, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Out of place competitor

parts.note: in racing to place is to finish in the first few; a runner who fails to do so is out of the places

explanation.surface: An athlete seems not to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of place' reads as 'not belonging', but in horse racing it means finishing outside the placed positions.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor who finishes unplaced in a race, so an unsuccessful entrant.

clue.text: Friday lunch for some makes a nutritious spread

explanation.surface: Some people's end-of-week midday repast makes a healthy feast.
explanation.walkthrough: Catholics traditionally eat fish on Friday; the ground dried fish is also spread on fields as fertiliser, so 'spread' is not a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friday dinner of seafood for Catholics, and ground fish used as fertiliser spread on soil.

clue.text: Bishop's remit for change

definitions.note: the possessive describes something belonging to a bishop, while the answer names that thing

indicators.note: to change these letters is to put them in a new order

explanation.surface: A bishop's area of responsibility is being altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges REMIT; the definition is a bishop's possession, his tall headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pointed headdress worn by a bishop belongs to him, hence the possessive.

clue.text: Gets lost, but may' be found at home in Battersea

definitions.text: be found at home in Battersea

explanation.surface: Something wanders off, yet turns up safe in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs and Cats Home in London takes in lost pets, so 'at home in Battersea' is that animal shelter, not someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander from one's path is to get lost, and homeless dogs and cats taken in at the Battersea shelter are wanderers too.

clue.text: Recesses for an art form

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alcoves are set aside to display a creative medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges AN ART; 'art form' reads as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy, cavities or chambers within bones such as the sinuses are recesses, and this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Brogue said to frighten birds away

indicators.note: said means spoken, so a word pronounced the same is wanted

parts.note: shoo is the cry used to drive birds off

explanation.surface: An Irish accent is used to scare off birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brogue' suggests an Irish accent, but it is also a sturdy leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a stout leather lace-up with punched decoration, a type of footwear.

clue.text: Demand payment out of turn

parts.note: ex means out of or former
an act is a turn, a performer's slot in a show

explanation.surface: Someone insists on being paid before their go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of turn' reads as an idiom for speaking improperly, but it splits into out and a stage turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a sum or tax is to insist on and obtain its payment.

clue.text: Cover up the firearms case

parts.note: a holster is the leather case for carrying a pistol

explanation.surface: Someone conceals the gun holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'Cover' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad and cover furniture with fabric is to upholster it.

clue.text: The frivolous one who gets ' Father Bear in trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A silly person lands a paternal bear in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' looks like one phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder and 'trouble' alone rearranges FATHER BEAR IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained, flighty person whose head seems as light as plumage is frivolous.
